doc.title: Bill Allred interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 24, 2017

title: Leaving Rock Island and auditioning for Disney in Miami
summary: Encouraged by Charlie Teagarden, he auditions in Miami with Jack Keller, Ray McKinley and Chubby Jackson and is offered a Disney spot.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And I really took to it. Because I hadn’t even started seventh grade yet was when our band program started. There was no sixth grade music back in 1940 something. And so I was playing “Jam On Home” you know which was bad for me because for me reading music came second or something I had to learn to do. I recall when I left Rock Island to — what I did, I had a chance to go out to Vegas a few times and I got to know Charlie Teagarden. At that time he was the secretary of the union in Las Vegas, but played in a lot of clubs and stuff like that. And his words to me, I’ll never forget this, I said, “Someday I want to have my own band and play all this Dixie stuff, but maybe play it with a little more complica — you know, do it with some charts and stuff like —.” They said, “Well you’ve got to get your ass out of Rock Island, first of all.” That’s a quote. Which later it came to pass and so anyway there’s all this talk about the new thing that’s going to be happening in Orlando. And Charlie Teagarden knew about it, a lot of the musicians that I knew in Rock Island and Davenport, that area, said boy you ought to look into that. So I just clipped a coupon from the union newspaper and I belonged to the union then. I sent a letter off and they said yes if you’d like to audition we’re having auditions at the — I forget which hotel it was — in Miami. So I lived in Rock Island. So I mustered up the money, and I was married then. I flew from Rock Island to Chicago to Miami, and they had an audition set up at a hotel down there. And they had two things. They had a big band set up with a couple of Disney music people from Anaheim of course. And they had a combo room, which is where I excelled. I mean I had been working on my reading purposely and so I did okay in the big band thing. I got through that all right. But I went into the combo room and here’s the band. They had a guy from © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-

Miami who was like the heavy piano player in Miami, a guy named Jack Keller. K-E-L- L-E-R. What a great piano player. On drums Ray McKinley. On bass Chubby Jackson. And I’m saying to myself holy shit, I mean like wow. I mean I played in the Navy band you know, so — when I was in the Navy from ’54 to ’57, so I met a few people but never got a chance to work with them. And so I played about an hour in the combo room. They said, “Do some more.” You know. And they’d invite this guy in. Sonny Anderson was a big Disney Entertainment guy then. And Jim Christenson ended up being the first band leader out here. And they liked what I did. And I was businessman enough to follow up with a letter saying boy, you know, I really enjoyed that and I said, I can see myself really fitting in. So I did get a letter back saying we really were impressed with what you did and our play would be to put you in the big marching band, which we intend to break up into smaller bands, a polka band, a sax quartet, a town band and a Dixieland band. And he said we of course like what you do as far as the Dixieland, and so that’s how I got on Disney. Well Disney didn’t move you or pay for your move, I mean we had to get there. So I had to sell a house and move two kids and a wife down to Orlando. Maybe this is too much Disney stuff.
